# Exact compensation for one common facet and a parallel middle cap circuit

This is a restricted, proved stress inequality. It does not assert that an
arbitrary critical circuit has the prescribed directions, or that an attained
unrestricted minimum is polytopal.

## 1. Hypotheses and conclusion

Let K0,K1,K2 be positive planar triangles with (K0+K2)/2 contained in K1.
Suppose the normalized joint cap/body stationarity of
candidate 11e10da90bca54a3 holds under independent affine
motions of all three triangles. Its cap multipliers are nonnegative. The
middle group consists of the three vertex-side caps parallel to K1's opposite
edges, through one interior anchor. At most one endpoint group has positive
multipliers; if present, it is the canonical centroid vertex-cap circuit
strictly isolated to that endpoint. All other cap multipliers vanish.

Assume precisely one middle compatibility facet has a positive multiplier
eta, and that its support faces in BOTH endpoint triangles are edges. Other
compatibility equalities are allowed, with zero multipliers. Then, with
gamma=4/9 and L1,Le the sums of the middle and endpoint cap multipliers,

    gamma (L1+Le) <= 2.                                      (1)

In fact the inequality is strict when eta>0. Here Le=0 if no endpoint group
is present. The proof includes every effective trace allowed by cap/body
coincidences. Combined with sum lambda=1/beta, (1) gives beta>=2/9 for this
stationary pattern.

## 2. Solving the middle affine equations

Number the middle vertices r1,r2,r3 so the stressed facet is opposite r3.
Write xi_i for barycentric coordinates, u_i=grad xi_i, and let the cap
anchor have positive barycentric coordinates alpha_i, summing to one.
The middle caps are xi_i>=alpha_i. Put A=area(K1), tau_i=1-alpha_i,
and w_i=lambda_i tau_i^2. Thus cap i has area A tau_i^2.

Let ell be the length of the stressed facet, n its outward unit normal,
and m its compatibility contact mean. Write m's barycentrics as
kappa=(kappa1,kappa2,0), where kappa1+kappa2=1. Because
n=-u3/|u3| and A|u3|=ell/2, put

    sigma=eta/(A|u3|)=2 eta/ell.

For arbitrary infinitesimal vertex motions delta r_k, direct change of
variables gives

    delta A = A sum_k u_k . delta r_k,
    delta cap_i = tau_i^2 delta A
       + A[2 alpha_i tau_i u_i.delta r_i
                 +tau_i^2 sum_(k!=i) u_i.delta r_k].           (2)

For completeness, the chord xi_i=alpha_i has constant xi_i=alpha_i and
mean xi_k=tau_i/2 for k!=i. Its coarea length is 2A tau_i. Adding its
boundary displacement to tau_i^2 delta A proves (2).

The central stress is delta A=sum_i lambda_i delta cap_i
-2 eta n.delta r(m). Divide by A and use sum_i u_i=0. With
T=sum_i w_i-1 and W=sum_i w_i u_i, the coefficient of delta r_k is

    W + [T+w_k(3 alpha_k-1)/(1-alpha_k)]u_k
            +2 sigma kappa_k u3 = 0.                         (3)

Dilation about the cap anchor also yields

    T=sigma alpha3.                                         (4)

The k=3 equation implies w1=w2=w, since u1,u2 are independent. The k=1,2
equations then give

    w-w3=2 sigma kappa1=2 sigma kappa2.

Since sigma>0, kappa1=kappa2=1/2 and w-w3=sigma. Thus m is exactly the
midpoint of the stressed middle edge. The remaining u1,u2 coefficients
in (3) imply alpha1=alpha2=p, because (3a-1)/(1-a) is strictly increasing
on (0,1). Necessarily alpha3=1-2p and 0<p<1/2. Equations (3),(4) become

    2 w p^2 = w3(1-2p)(1-p),
    w(1+2p)+2w3(1-p)=1.

Solving gives the exact identities

    w=1-2p,                   w3=2p^2/(1-p),
    sigma=(1-3p)/(1-p),       0<p<1/3,
    lambda1=lambda2=(1-2p)/(1-p)^2,
    lambda3=1/[2(1-p)],
    L1=(5-9p)/[2(1-p)^2].                                  (5)

No zero-multiplier exception was discarded: if one middle multiplier is
zero then all are zero by the positive circuit threshold equations. That
would make (3) impossible for k=1,2, so the middle weights are positive.

The same formulas extend continuously to sigma=0,p=1/3; alternatively the
previous zero-contact weighted-chord lemma gives L1<=9/4 directly.

## 3. Exact facet trace budgets

Call the deepest endpoint, if present, e, and the other f. Let their
supported edges in direction n have positive lengths ell_e,ell_f. Their
Minkowski average is an interval I in the stressed middle edge, so

    ell_e+ell_f <= 2 ell.                                   (6)

It contains m, the midpoint of the middle edge.

Let W1,We,Wf denote the integrals over these three edges of the sum of
middle cap multipliers times their effective cap traces. At proper edge
intersections the trace is the ordinary indicator. At a coincident cap
and body edge it is the measurable theta in [0,1] used by the normalized
stress. Moving only the supported edge parallel while fixing the other
two supporting lines is an affine triangle motion, in both signs.
Applying stationarity to these three motions gives

    W1=ell+2 eta,
    We=(1-gamma Le)ell_e-eta,
    Wf=ell_f-eta.                                           (7)

To justify the own-endpoint term, the canonical centroid circuit has equal
lambda values: its positive dependence weights are proportional to the
three opposite-edge lengths, and each proper chord has two thirds of that
edge's length, so lambda_j S_j=rho_j t forces equality. On any one triangle
edge, two of the centroid vertex caps each occupy length (2/3)ell_e, while
the third occupies zero. Their combined weighted trace is therefore
(Le/3)(4/3)ell_e=gamma Le ell_e. The isolating caps at this endpoint
strictly exclude the other two fibers. These facts prove all of (7).

## 4. A midpoint trace inequality with the exact location retained

Parameterize the supported endpoint edges affinely and in the same
orientation by x_e(s),x_f(s), 0<=s<=1. Their midpoints uniformly parameterize
I. For every ambient halfspace H, if its midpoint belongs to H, at least
one endpoint belongs to H. For middle caps 1 and 2, the normals are not
parallel to the stressed edge, so boundaries have length zero on all three
edges and this proves the usual indicator inequality almost everywhere.
Middle cap 3 misses the entire middle edge, because xi3=0<alpha3; its
midpoint contribution is zero, and its two endpoint effective traces are
nonnegative even if a cap/body edge coincides. Consequently,

    average_I(middle weighted cap profile)
                      <= We/ell_e + Wf/ell_f.                (8)

Parameterize the middle edge by t=xi1 in [0,1], so xi2=1-t. Put
lambda=lambda1=lambda2. By (5), its weighted cap profile is

    w(t)=lambda[1_(t>=p)+1_(t<=1-p)].                         (9)

Its whole-edge average is 2 lambda(1-p). Every subinterval of [0,1]
containing 1/2 has average at least this value. Here is an explicit proof:
the profile is symmetric, and for x in [0,1/2],

    integral_x^(1/2) [w(t)-2lambda(1-p)] dt
       = lambda(1-2p)x                    if 0<=x<=p,
       = 2lambda p(1/2-x)                 if p<=x<=1/2.

Both expressions are nonnegative. Add the two symmetric half-interval
identities to obtain the claim for any interval containing 1/2. Since
m in I, (8) therefore implies

    1+sigma = W1/ell <= We/ell_e+Wf/ell_f
             =2-gamma Le-eta(1/ell_e+1/ell_f).               (10)

The reciprocal-length inequality and (6) give

    1/ell_e+1/ell_f >= 4/(ell_e+ell_f) >= 2/ell.

Using sigma=2eta/ell in (10),

    gamma Le <= 1-2sigma.                                  (11)

Thus the endpoint middle-cap traces, not only the contact multiplier,
pay for the extra middle multiplier budget.

## 5. The final rational inequality

Substitute (5) into the difference between the proposed bound and (11):

    1-gamma L1+2sigma
       =(1-3p)(17-21p)/[9(1-p)^2] >=0.                     (12)

It follows that gamma(L1+Le)<=gamma L1+1-2sigma<=2.
For eta>0, p<1/3, both factors in the numerator of (12) are positive,
so the last inequality is strict. Every estimate used here is exact.

This settles this one common-facet, facet-parallel-middle-circuit stress
pattern only. Two stressed facets or rotated middle cap directions are
not covered by the profile identity (9).
